title: Classification and mutation prediction from non-small cell lung cancer histopathology images using deep learning

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Classification and mutation prediction from non-small cell lung cancer histopathology images using deep learning》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Visual inspection of histopathology slides is one of the main methods used by pathologists to assess the stage, type and subtype of lung tumors.

evidence.text: Visual inspection of histopathology slides is one of the main methods used by pathologists to assess the stage, type and subtype of lung tumors.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Classification and mutation prediction from non-small cell lung cancer histopathology images using deep learning》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】In this study, we trained a deep convolutional neural network (inception v3) on whole-slide images obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas to accurately and automatically classify them into LUAD, LUSC or normal lung tissue.

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】Furthermore, we trained the network to predict the ten most commonly mutated genes in LUAD.

evidence.text: In this study, we trained a deep convolutional neural network (inception v3) on whole-slide images obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas to accurately and automatically classify them into LUAD, LUSC or normal lung tissue.
Furthermore, we trained the network to predict the ten most commonly mutated genes in LUAD.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Classification and mutation prediction from non-small cell lung cancer histopathology images using deep learning》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】The performance of our method is comparable to that of pathologists, with an average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.97.

【Abstract · abstract-1-7】We found that six of them-STK11, EGFR, FAT1, SETBP1, KRAS and TP53-can be predicted from pathology images, with AUCs from 0.733 to 0.856 as measured on a held-out population.

evidence.text: The performance of our method is comparable to that of pathologists, with an average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.97.
We found that six of them-STK11, EGFR, FAT1, SETBP1, KRAS and TP53-can be predicted from pathology images, with AUCs from 0.733 to 0.856 as measured on a held-out population.
